title: Pacer: quantum arrival granularity labnotes
content:
Notes to self - pacer / quantum arrival granularity experiments

Goal
- Explore how small-scale, high-frequency pulses ("quantum" arrivals: 1-5 reqs bursts every 50-200ms) interact with batching/kv-cache when mixed with background bulk requests. Want to characterize tail behavior and compound effects when model variants are switched under load.

Hypothesis
- Very short, tightly spaced pulses cause batching to either: (a) increase latency due to waiting window expiry, or (b) cause micro-batching that increases GPU context switches when combined with full-size requests.
- Quantized model (int8) should reduce per-token compute, but may amplify GC or memory thrash if allocator behavior differs.

Environment
- Cluster: staging-dedicated-3 (4xA100-80GB nodes), driver image: rwinf/serving:2025-02-05
- Runtime flags: --batch-window-ms=8 --max-batch=64 --kv-cache-enabled=true --prefill-strategy=on-demand
- Models: llama-open-13b-v1 (fp16), llama-open-13b-v1-q8 (int8 dynamic)
- Load generator: loadgen-v2 (commit 9f3a2), experiments orchestrated via bench-ctl.

Key commands (repro steps)
- start server: ./deploy.sh --env=staging-dedicated-3 --image=rwinf/serving:2025-02-05
- run arrival pattern: loadgen-v2 --pattern="quantum:burst=3,interval=120ms" --mix="background:30req/s,context=1024" --model=llama-open-13b-v1 --duration=900s --out=runA.json
- quantized run: same command with --model=llama-open-13b-v1-q8 -> runB.json
- capture traces: bench-ctl trace collect --run=runA --span=serve,kvcache,prefill --out=traceA.zip

Observation summary (high-level)
- RunA (fp16): p50 ~ 36ms, p95 ~ 122ms, p99 ~ 310ms, p999 ~ 1.2s. Spikes at p999 correlated with short GC-like pauses in host process (saw ephemeral 70-120ms blocking in GPU feeder thread).
- RunB (q8): p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 98ms, p99 ~ 260ms, p999 ~ 1.45s. Lower central tendencies, but fatter extreme tail. Observed repeated kernel rebinds and occasional memory pressure signals on node (OOM-kick avoided but elevated allocation churn).
- KV cache hit-rate: baseline 84% on RunA, 78% on RunB (quantized runs appear to trigger slightly different tokenization/serialization path causing lower reuse).

Representative ascii charts (latency distribution sketch)
- RunA latency buckets (ms): |=====|====|==|=|    |      | 
  p50   p75  p90 p95 p99  p999  outliers
- RunB latency buckets (ms): |=======|=====|===|==|   |       |
  (notice more mass earlier, but more extreme final outliers)

Trace snippets (not exhaustive)
- traceA: 2025-02-10T15:03:21Z - feeder thread backpressure 84ms -> batching window extended -> request waited for next cycle; those requests show increased end-to-end latency.
- traceB: 2025-02-10T15:07:42Z - kernel rebind 130ms while another small burst arrives; GPU idle/wakeup pattern leads to context switch overhead.

Detailed notes / interesting artifacts
- Prefill behavior: on-demand prefill avoids bulk cache priming cost but means first-of-context requests pay more; quantum pulses increase chance of sequential cache misses because pulses often carry short, distinct prompts. Consider light-weight prefetch for short sessions (heuristic: if pulse length < 8 tokens, prefetch next 32 tokens from kv-cache?).
- Batching window: 8ms seemed borderline — increased to 12ms moved some p95->p99 mass down but increased median by ~6ms. Suggest exploration of adaptive window: widen after consecutive bursts, shrink during lull.
- Quantization side effects: q8 runtime path uses different allocator pools; combined with small bursts the allocator shares more frequently causing CPU-side stalls. Need to instrument malloc arenas and run with jemalloc stats.
- Network: no obvious cross-node saturation; spikes correlate with process-local events.

Quick reproducible micro-experiment
- 1) Launch single node with --batch-window-ms=6, --max-batch=48, model fp16.
- 2) Run: loadgen-v2 --pattern="quantum:burst=2,interval=70ms" --mix="background:10req/s,context=256" --duration=300s --out=quickA.json
- 3) Switch model to q8 in place (hot-swap via bench-ctl) and run same pattern -> quickB.json
- Expected: quickA central latencies slightly higher but fewer p999 events than quickB.

Open questions / next steps
- Is the p999 tail dominated by allocator pauses or by kernel scheduling? Need deeper sampling of CPU stacks during the spikes. Plan: perf record on feeder and allocator threads during a targeted 5m window.
- Can we add a micro-prefetch layer that primes KV cache for repeated short-session tokens without full prefill cost? Prototype idea: track recent pulse token signatures and prefetch likely next token embedding chunks for 200ms after pulse.
- Evaluate adaptive batch-window heuristic: implement a simple exponential backoff where repeated pulses widen the window up to 24ms, decay over 1s of idle. Measure net token-cost vs latency tradeoffs.
- Try jemalloc + tcmalloc vs default to see if arena fragmentation is a root cause.

Personal notes (scratchy)
- Heard from Ravi that this pattern appears in mobile-triggered assistant queries (short bursts while background syncs run). Lower p50 matters less than p999 for UX here.
- Leah flagged that some enterprise customers see increased admonishment when tail spikes coincide with A/B rollout of larger context models. Good to test variant fallthroughs under quantum load.

Action items
- [ ] Run jemalloc instrumented runs for q8 path (assigned: Emilia) — due 2025-02-14
- [ ] Implement quick adaptive-window PoC in bench branch (assigned: Ravi) — due 2025-02-18
- [ ] Perf stack capture during 3 targeted runs (assigned: Leah) — due 2025-02-13

End of notes.

Random scratch: maybe call this "pacer" because pulses behave like pacemaker spikes; want to correlate with real traffic sample from mobile cohort next sprint.
